title: Introduce invocation-bridge: sampled context bundles and compact cost heatmap
author: Maya Chen
ci_status: pass (initial unit test failure fixed, rerun passed)
description:
Summary: Adds an "invocation-bridge" pipeline component that stitches sampled traces, compacted structured log bundles, and token-level cost rollups into a small footprint index and a compact cost heatmap dashboard. Motivation: long-tail cost & debugging is dominated by a small fraction of invocations where context and prefetching patterns matter; existing rollups either lost context or were too large to query interactively. This PR introduces a lightweight joiner that keeps a bounded set of context anchors per invocation and exposes a compact heatmap view for per-route token-cost vs latency slices.

What this changes (single continuous description): The PR adds a new background worker (invocation-bridge) that consumes sampled traces and structured log bundles, attaches up to N context anchors (prompt prefix signature, KV-prefetch hint, first-k tokens fingerprint) and writes a compact invocation index and a small per-invocation token-cost histogram. On the query surface we add a new dashboard panel (Compact Cost Heatmap) that allows slicing by route, model variant, and prefetch hint label. The change also introduces: 1) a small on-disk serialization format for context bundles (compact protobuf v2) used by the bridge, 2) a KV-prefetch signal extractor that tags invocations when prefetch calls were observed, 3) two new metrics (invocation.bridge.latency_ms and invocation.bridge.join_rate) and two tracing tags (bridge.context_count, bridge-prefetch).

Design notes and tradeoffs: The bridge intentionally keeps per-invocation state bounded (configurable default anchors=4) to avoid explosion in storage and index cardinality. We opted for a compact histogram (8 fixed buckets, 4-bit counts) to keep payloads small and make heatmap rollups cheap. The sampling strategy is layered: input traces are sampled by the existing adaptive sampler; the bridge then applies a deterministic shingle-based sampling to ensure coverage of long-tail prompt patterns. We prioritized read/query performance for the dashboard over storing full logs; full log lookup remains available via an index pointer.

Checklist:
- [x] Bridge worker implementation and tests (invocation_bridge/*)
- [x] Compact context proto and serializers
- [x] Extractor for KV-prefetch and prompt-fingerprint
- [x] Migration that backfills for last 30 days (limited to traces sampled)
- [x] Dashboard JSON + per-route slice queries
- [x] CI and e2e smoke tests
- [x] Documentation notes (observability/bridge.md)

Rollout plan: feature gate off by default for existing clusters. Admins can enable via telemetry.feature.invocation_bridge=true. We will run the bridge in a canary mode for 48h in staging and then enable for 10% of production traffic for two weeks (monitor invocation.bridge.join_rate, new metric error rate, and SLO delta). Backfill job is optional and rate-limited (configurable) to prevent overload.

Migration notes: No breaking schema changes. The bridge writes new compact artifacts under telemetry/invocation_bridge/{tenant}/{date}/. The backfill job is idempotent. If feature is disabled, dashboards will gracefully hide panels.

Security & privacy: Context bundles are stripped of PII by the existing log-sanitizer step; we added an extra scrub stage for any key/value pairs in prefetched objects. Artifacts written are ACL'd to tenant storage and follow current retention policies.

Observability additions: metrics: invocation.bridge.latency_ms, invocation.bridge.join_rate, invocation.bridge.backfill_progress. Logs: invocation_bridge.INFO events for join start/finish and failure reasons. Traces: added bridge.* span names and tags described above. Dashboards: dashboards/compact_cost_heatmap.json (panel, query templates, drilldowns to invocation detail).

Performance: Local benchmarks show bridge adds ~1.1% CPU and ~100ms background processing per sampled trace at default anchors=4. Storage overhead estimated at ~3% increase for sampled trace artifacts (configurable via anchors and histogram density).

Related work: complements existing prefix-warmup traces and token-cost rollups (see ENG-4012). This is intentionally compact to serve interactive SRE workflows without full trace rehydration.

review_comments: Evan Park: Nice incremental design. Two asks: (1) make anchors configurable per-tenant (not just cluster) and (2) add a short-circuit when no prefetch signals are present to avoid unnecessary writes.
Maya Chen (author): Added per-tenant override via tenant.config.telemetry.invocation_bridge. Added prefetch short-circuit; updated tests to cover both paths.

Sophie Rivera: Dashboard looks useful. Request: default time-range should be 6h and add a route-level color scale that is consistent across time windows. Also flagged a query that could scan full index; recommend adding a tenant+date prefix filter.
Maya Chen (author): Updated dashboard JSON to default to 6h and added stable color scale. Added tenant+date prefix in queries and included a note in docs about cost of wider time range.
Arjun Patel: Found a flake in test_worker where a timing assumption made the test brittle. Suggested using a fake clock.
Maya Chen (author): Reworked tests to use the test clock harness; CI flake resolved.
SRE Review (automated): Confirmed the backfill job's throttling knobs and monitoring targets.
